strengths: Addresses practical deployment complexity of existing speculative decoding methods (trained models, maintenance, domain shift) with a training-free alternative

Comprehensive experimental evaluation across multiple models (8B/70B/14B scales), diverse datasets (reasoning, coding, conversation, long-context), and realistic batch sizes with proper latency-throughput curves
Demonstrates strong robustness: cold-start speedup (1.1-1.23×), rapid multilingual adaptation (1.6-1.8× within 1,000 conversations), and superior long-context stability
Rigorous hardware-aware analysis using roofline modeling (Section 3.2, Appendix B) to derive speculation length selection formula with clear theoretical grounding
Clear presentation with effective visualizations and reproducible implementation (code to be released, detailed pseudocode)
weaknesses: Limited algorithmic novelty: combines existing techniques (n-gram matching from PLD/REST, trie from Lookahead, roofline analysis from Williams et al. 2009) without fundamental innovation; main difference from Lookahead is avoiding pruning

Mixed performance results undermine competitiveness claims: EAGLE-3 consistently outperforms on Llama-3.3-70B English (Figure 6), with explanation provided but this weakens the core contribution narrative

Datastore requirement is a hidden complexity contradicting 'training-free' framing: requires 13 GB storage, pre-seeding or online accumulation, with modest cold-start gains (1.1×) and unquantified privacy/latency costs

Insufficient ablation and sensitivity analysis: scaling factors determined by unspecified grid search with no details on hyperparameter space, generalization, or sensitivity; fixed hyperparameters (P=4, 100 samples) lack justification

CPU overhead uncharacterized: background trie/suffix array operations lack quantitative analysis; no evaluation of CPU saturation impact or CPU-constrained deployment scenarios despite being acknowledged limitation

Venue fit concern: primarily a systems/infrastructure contribution applying standard techniques to LLM inference; limited computational linguistics novelty; would be better suited to systems venues (OSDI, ASPLOS, VLDB)

Long-context advantage claims unsupported: Table 1 shows 1.23-1.26× speedup on PG-19, lower than short-context (1.8-2.3×); authors acknowledge 'SGLang kernels limit achievable gains,' suggesting system-level, not algorithmic, limitations
Statistical rigor lacking: five runs with averages only, no confidence intervals or significance tests; noisy figures (especially Figure 3) without error bars or standard deviations

Incomplete baseline comparisons: Lookahead evaluated in mismatched 'warm' vs 'cold' scenarios; both SSSD and REST use same datastore but algorithm may inherently suit certain data distributions better
Limited architecture coverage: MoE and MLA models relegated to Limitations without quantification; evaluation primarily on Llama family with unclear generalization to Mistral, Gemma, Phi, etc.

strengths: Clear practical motivation addressing real deployment complexity of speculative decoding
Comprehensive experimental evaluation across multiple models, tasks, and settings with realistic SGLang integration
Exceptional multilingual and cold-start results (1.6-1.8× after 1000 conversations for new languages; 1.1-1.23× from empty datastore)
Solid hardware-aware analysis grounded in roofline model with detailed FLOPS/IO breakdown
Competitive or superior performance to EAGLE-3 and other training-based methods across diverse benchmarks
Thoughtful system design with complementary data sources and efficient suffix-array implementation
Strong results on out-of-distribution tasks where training-based draft models degrade
weaknesses: Limited algorithmic novelty: combines existing techniques (suffix arrays, n-grams, roofline model) without fundamental innovation
Experimental fairness concerns: EAGLE/Lookahead use default parameters while SSSD is tuned; Lookahead warm-up disabled due to SGLang implementation
Heavy dependence on accumulated datastore: cold-start speedup (1.1-1.23×) is modest, performance scales logarithmically with datastore size
Modest practical gains at realistic batch sizes: speedups decrease to 1.3-1.4× at batch size 32, limiting impact in high-throughput production scenarios
Incomplete ablations on design choices: discount factors (0.6), prefix length (P=4), weight sensitivity, and cross-model transfer of learned weights
Unclear generalization: claimed weights transfer across models/tasks but limited evidence provided; see varying performance in Figure 5
Long-context benefits unclear: absolute gains modest (1.23× vs 0.80× for EAGLE-3); unclear if baseline underperforms due to kernels vs. algorithm
Missing analysis of failure modes: MoE/MLA limitations acknowledged but not empirically explored; CPU bottleneck mentioned but never quantified
Reproducibility details underspecified: sampling heuristics ('typically 100'), Magpie procedure, grid search details, temperature/top-p sensitivity
